Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 22, verse 35:

﴿Those who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts tremble﴾ they fear Him out of awe, ﴿and the patient ones over what afflicts them﴾ of trials and calamities, ﴿and those who establish the prayer﴾ at its appointed times, ﴿and from what We have provided for them they spend﴾ they give in charity.

**﴿And the camels﴾**: the plural of *budnah*, so called because of the greatness of its body (*badan*). In the Sharia (sacred law), the term covers camels and cattle. It is also read with the *rafʿ* (nominative vowel), *wal-budnu*, and this is like His saying ﴿And the moon—We have determined it﴾ [Yā-Sīn: 39].

**﴿We have made them for you among the symbols of God﴾**: that is, among the markers of the Sharia (*aʿlām al-sharīʿah*) which God has prescribed. Attributing them to His name is a glorification of them. *Min shaʿāʾir Allāh* is the second object of *jaʿalnā*, the verb's two objects being *hā* and *min shaʿāʾir Allāh*.

**﴿For you in them is good﴾**: benefit in this world and reward in the next.

**﴿So mention the name of God over them﴾**: at the time of slaughtering them.

**﴿Standing in rows﴾**: a *ḥāl* (circumstantial qualifier) of the *hāʾ* (the pronoun referring to them), meaning: standing, having arranged their forelegs and hind legs.

**﴿Then when their sides fall﴾**: *wujūb al-junūb* is their sides falling to the ground, from *wajaba al-ḥāʾiṭ wajbah*, when the wall collapsed. That is, when their sides have fallen to the ground after slaughter and their movement has stopped.

**﴿Then eat from them﴾**: if you wish.

**﴿And feed the one who is content and the one who is in need﴾**: *al-qāniʿ* is the one who asks, from *qanaʿtu ilayhi* when you humble yourself to him and ask him (*qunūʿan*). **﴿The one in need﴾** is the one who shows himself and presents himself but does not ask. It has also been said that *al-qāniʿ* is the one who is content with what he has and with what is given to him without asking, from *qanitu qunʿan wa qanāʿah*, while *al-muʿtarr* is the one who presents himself to be asked.

**﴿Thus We have subjected them to you﴾**: that is, just as We commanded you to slaughter them for yourselves. Or it is like His saying ﴿That [is so]; and whoever honours﴾ [al-Ḥajj: 32]. Then He resumed and said, *sakhkharnāhā lakum*, meaning: We made them submissive to you despite their strength and the greatness of their bodies, so that you could slaughter them.

**﴿So that you may be grateful﴾**: so that you may thank God for His favour upon you.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 22, verse 37:

﴿Their flesh will never reach God, nor their blood, but it is piety from you that reaches Him.﴾ That is: God will never accept the flesh and the blood, but He accepts piety. Or: it is not the flesh given in charity nor the blood shed at the sacrifice that attains the good pleasure of God; rather, the meaning is those who offer sacrifices and draw near (to God). The meaning is: those who sacrifice and draw near will not gain their Lord's pleasure except through observing the intention, sincerity, and maintaining the conditions of piety. It has been said: the people of the Jahiliyyah, when they slaughtered camels, would sprinkle the blood around the House (the Kaʿbah) and smear it with blood. When the Muslims performed the Hajj, they wished to do the same, and so this was revealed: ﴿Thus He has subjected them to you﴾, that is, the camels (al-budn), ﴿so that you may magnify God﴾, that is, so that you mention the name of God at the time of slaughter, or so that you glorify God (al-takbir, "magnifying"), ﴿for having guided you﴾, that is, for having directed you to it. ﴿And give good news to the doers of good﴾, those who comply with His commands, of reward.

The verb "yadfa'u" is the reading of Makki and Basri and others, while "yudafi'u" means that He goes to great lengths in defending them, ﴿against those who believe﴾, meaning He averts the harm of the polytheists from the believers, and similar to it is ﴿Indeed, We shall surely help Our messengers and those who believe﴾ [Ghafir: 51]. Then he gave the reason for that in His words, ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love every treacherous one﴾ in the trust of Allah, ﴿ungrateful﴾ for the blessing of Allah, meaning (p-443) because He does not love their opposites, who are the treacherous ones who betray Allah and the Messenger, betray their trusts, disbelieve in the blessings of Allah, and deny them.

﴿Permission is given﴾: Madani, Basri and Asim read it as ﴿أُذِنَ﴾. ﴿To those who are being fought﴾: Madani, Shami and Hafs read ﴿يُقاتَلُونَ﴾ with a fatha on the ta. The meaning is: permission was given to them to fight, and the object of the permission, "fighting," was omitted because of the indication in ﴿يُقاتَلُونَ﴾ (they are being fought). ﴿Because they were wronged﴾: meaning, because they were oppressed. They were the Companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). "The polytheists of Makkah used to harm them with severe harm, and they would come to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) from among those who had been beaten and wounded, complaining of their oppression to him. He would say to them: 'Be patient, for I have not been commanded to fight,' until he emigrated, and then this verse was revealed." This is the first verse in which permission to fight was granted, after fighting had been forbidden in some seventy-odd verses. ﴿And indeed God is able to give them victory﴾: that is, to give victory to the believers, ﴿Able﴾ meaning capable. This is good news to the believers of victory, and it is similar to His saying: ﴿Indeed, God defends those who have believed﴾ [al-Hajj: 38].

**Al-Nasafi's commentary (Madarik al-Tanzil) on Surah al-Hajj, verse 40:**

﴿Alladhina﴾ is in the genitive case as a substitute (badal, apposition) for "alladhina," or in the accusative with the implied verb "a'ni" (I mean), or in the nominative by implying "hum" (they). ﴿Who have been expelled from their homes﴾ in Makkah ﴿without right, only because they say: "Our Lord is Allah."﴾ That is, without any cause other than monotheism, which should have been the cause for their being established, not the cause for their expulsion. A similar verse is ﴿Do you resent us only because we believed in Allah?﴾ [al-Ma'idah 5:59]. The position of "an yaqulu" (that they say) is in the genitive as a substitute for "haqq" (right). The meaning is: they were expelled from their homes only because of their saying (this).

﴿And had it not been for Allah's repelling﴾ "difa'" (repelling) is read by Madani, and by Ya'qub as ﴿dafa'u⁠ — the people, some by means of others, they would have been destroyed﴾, and with the lighter reading (lahuddimat) it is read by the Hijazi reader ﴿monasteries, churches, synagogues, and mosques﴾. That is: had it not been for His manifesting [His religion] and empowering the Muslims over the disbelievers through struggle (mujahadah), the polytheists would have prevailed over the adherents of the different religions in their times and over their places of worship, and they would have demolished them, leaving the Christians no churches and their monks no monasteries, nor the Muslims any mosques. Or [the meaning is that] the polytheists would have prevailed over the community of Muhammad (ﷺ), over the Muslims, and over the People of the Book who are under their protection (dhimmah), and they would have demolished the places of worship of both groups. He mentioned "other than the mosques" before them because of their earlier existence, or because of their proximity to demolition. ﴿In which the name of Allah is much mentioned﴾ refers either to the mosques or to everything mentioned above. ﴿Allah will surely help those who help Him﴾ That is, who help His religion and His allies. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Powerful﴾ over supporting His allies, ﴿Almighty﴾ over exacting vengeance on His enemies.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 22, verse 41:

﴿Those who﴾: its position (maḥall) is in the accusative as a substitute (badal) for "whoever helps Him," or in the genitive as a follower (tābiʿ) of "those who were expelled." ﴿If We establish them firmly in the land, they establish the prayer, give the zakat, enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong﴾: this is a report from Allah about what the conduct (sīrah) of the emigrants will be if He establishes them firmly in the land and expands for them in the world. How could they uphold the matter of the religion otherwise? In it is evidence for the correctness of the command of the Rightly Guided Caliphs (al-Khulafāʾ al-Rāshidūn), because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, gave them power (tamkīn) and the execution of command together with a just conduct. And from al-Ḥasan: they are the community (ummah) of Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿And to Allah belongs the outcome of affairs﴾: that is, their return is to His judgment and decree. In it is an affirmation of what He promised of the manifestation of His friends and the elevation of His word.

﴿And if they deny you﴾ — this is consolation for Muhammad (ﷺ) regarding the denial of him by the people of Makkah; that is, you are not alone in denial. ﴿Then the people of Nuh (Noah) denied before them﴾ — before your people — ﴿Nuh﴾ (Noah) ﴿and ʿAd﴾ denied Hud ﴿and Thamud﴾ denied Salih.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 22, verse 43:

﴿And the people of Abraham﴾ [denied] Abraham, ﴿and the people of Lot﴾ [denied] Lot.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 22, verse 44:

﴿And the people of Madyan﴾ (that is, the people of Shu'ayb), ﴿and Musa was denied﴾. Pharaoh and the Copts denied him. (p-445) He did not say "and the people of Musa," because Musa was not denied by his own people, the Children of Israel; rather, he was denied by others than his people. Or it is as if it was said, after mentioning the denial of every nation of its messenger: "And Musa was also denied, despite the clarity of his signs and the manifestness of his miracles, so what do you think about others?" ﴿Then I gave the disbelievers respite﴾, that is, I granted them time and delayed their punishment. ﴿Then I seized them﴾, that is, I punished them for their disbelief. ﴿So how was My rejection﴾, that is, My disapproval and My alteration, when I replaced for them blessings with afflictions, life with destruction, and prosperity with ruin. "Nakiri" (My rejection) with the ya' in both pause and continuation is read by Ya'qub (Ya'qub al-Hadrami).

﴿So how many a town did We destroy﴾. "We destroyed it" (*ahlaktuha*) is the reading of the Basrans. ﴿while it was a wrongdoer﴾ is a circumstantial clause (*hal*), meaning: and its people were polytheists. ﴿So it lies fallen﴾, meaning fallen down, from *khawa al-najm*, when the star falls. ﴿upon its roofs﴾ is connected to *khawiyah*. The meaning is that it has fallen upon its roofs, that is, its roofs collapsed to the ground, then its walls fell down and came to rest on top of the roofs. ﴿So it lies fallen﴾ has no place in the i'rab (grammatical analysis), because it is conjoined to *ahlaktuha*, and this verb has no place in i'rab. This holds when we make *ka'ayyin* (how many) in the accusative position, with the estimate "many towns did We destroy." ﴿And a well abandoned﴾, meaning left unattended because its bucket and rope have been lost and its upkeep has been neglected, or it may be that the water is still there and the tools for drawing water are with it, but it has been left idle (*'uttilat*), meaning abandoned and not drawn from, because its people have perished. ﴿And a lofty palace﴾, plastered with gypsum (*mujassas*), from *al-shayd*, which is gypsum (*al-jiss*), or raised in its construction, from *shad al-bina'*, meaning he raised the building. The meaning is: how many a town have We destroyed, how many a well have We left idle of its drawers, and how many a lofty palace have We emptied of its residents! That is, We destroyed both the desert and the settled areas together, so the palaces were left without their owners and the wells without those who came to them. The more apparent view is that "well" and "palace" are meant in a general sense.

The commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 22, verse 46:

﴿Have they not travelled through the land?﴾ This is an exhortation to travel, so that they may see the places where those whom Allah destroyed for their disbelief were laid low, and witness their remains, and so take heed (ya'tabiru). ﴿So that they may have hearts with which they understand, or ears with which they hear.﴾ That is: they understand what must be understood of the Oneness (tawhid) and the like, and hear (p-446) what must be heard of the Revelation (wahy).

﴿For indeed it is not the eyes that are blinded, but it is the hearts within the breasts that are blinded.﴾ The pronoun in "fa-innaha" is the pronoun of the matter (damir al-qissa), or an ambiguous pronoun explained by "al-absar" (the eyes). That is: their eyes have not gone blind to seeing, but their hearts have gone blind to taking heed (i'tibar). Every person has four eyes: two eyes in his head and two eyes in his heart. So if he sees with what is in the heart and is blind with what is in the head, it does not harm him; and if he sees with what is in the head and is blind with what is in the heart, it does not benefit him. He mentioned "the breasts" (al-sudur) to clarify that the seat of knowledge is the heart, and lest it be said that "the heart" (al-qalb) means something other than this organ, as one says "the heart is the core (lubb) of everything."

They ask you to hasten the punishment (al-'ajil, the appointed punishment) in mockery. ﴿And Allah will not fail His promise.﴾ It is as if he had said: Why do they ask you to hasten it? It is as though they consider escape from it possible. Failing to keep a promise is only conceivable in the case of one whose promise may be broken. ﴿And Allah will not fail His promise﴾, and what He has promised will surely befall them, even if after a while. ﴿And indeed a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of what you count.﴾ "Ya'udduna" (they count) is read by Makki and by the Kufans other than Asim, meaning: how can they ask to hasten the punishment of One for whom a single day of His punishment spans a thousand years of your years, because the days of hardship are long.

And how many a town did I give respite while it was wrongdoing—that is, how many people of towns who were wrongdoers like you I gave respite for a time—then I seized it with punishment; and to Me is the final return. That is, the return is to Me, so nothing escapes Me.

As for the first (فَكَأيِّنْ, with fa'), it is connected by the fa' particle, and this one (وكَأيِّنْ, with waw) is different because the first came as a substitute (badal) for فَكَيْفَ كانَ نَكِيرِ ("so how was My rejection?"). As for this one, its ruling is the ruling of the two sentences preceding it that are conjoined by waw, namely ﴿ولَنْ يُخْلِفَ اللهُ وعْدَهُ﴾ ("And Allah will never fail His promise") and ﴿وإنَّ يَوْمًا عِنْدَ رَبِّكَ﴾ ("And indeed a day with your Lord is like a thousand years").

Say: "O mankind, I am only a clear warner to you." Why did He not say "a bringer of good news and a warner" (bashir wa nadhir)? Because of the mention of the two groups after it: the discourse is directed at the polytheists, and "O mankind" is a call addressed to them, and they are the ones of whom it was said, "Have they not travelled through the earth?" and they were described as being hasty for the punishment. The believers and their reward were inserted only so that they (the disbelievers) would be enraged; or its implied sense is: "a clear warner, and a bringer of good news," so he gave good news first and then said...

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 22, verse 50:

﴿So those who believe and do righteous deeds—for them is forgiveness﴾ for their sins, ﴿and a generous provision﴾, i.e., a good one. Then he warned, saying:

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 22, verse 51:

﴿And those who strive﴾ sa'a fi amr fulan (to strive regarding someone's affair) means to ruin it by one's striving. ﴿Against Our signs﴾, i.e., the Qur'an, ﴿seeking to frustrate them﴾ (mu'ajizin) is a circumstantial clause (hal). It is read mu'ajjizin (with shaddah on the ayn) by Makki and Abu 'Amr. 'Ajazahu means he competed with him, as if each of the two was trying to make the other unable to catch up with him. When one outstrips the other, it is said a'jazahu and 'ajjazahu. The meaning is: they strove to corrupt its meaning by attacking it, calling it sorcery, poetry and fables, competing with one another in their claim and their scheming, hoping that their plot against Islam would succeed for them. ﴿Those are the companions of the Blazing Fire﴾, i.e., the kindled Fire.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 22, verse 52:

﴿And We did not send before you﴾ *min* here marks the starting point of the action. ﴿any messenger﴾ *min* here is extra (*za'ida*), used to emphasize the negation. ﴿or any prophet﴾. This is clear evidence for the distinction between the messenger (*rasul*) and the prophet (*nabi*), contrary to the view of some who say they are one and the same. The Prophet (ﷺ) was asked about the prophets, and he said: "They number one hundred and twenty-four thousand." It was then asked: "How many of them were messengers?" He said: "Three hundred and thirteen."

The difference between them is that the messenger is one who, along with a miracle (*mu'jiza*), was given a Book revealed to him, whereas the prophet is one to whom no Book was revealed, and who was only commanded to call people to the law (*shari'a*) of the one before him. It has also been said that the messenger is the one who establishes a law, and the prophet is the one who preserves the law of another.

﴿Except when he wishes﴾: *taman-na* here means "he recited," as the poet says:

*He wished for God's Book on the first night,*
*as David wished for the Psalms with ease.*

﴿Satan cast into his wish﴾, meaning into his recitation. It has been said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) was in the assembly of his people reciting *al-Najm* [53:1]. When he reached His words *'And Manat, the third, the other'* [53:20], there flowed upon his tongue: *'Those are the exalted cranes, and their intercession is to be hoped for.'* He did not notice it until the infallibility (*'ismah*) overtook him, and he became aware of it." It has also been said that Gabriel (peace be upon him) alerted him, and he informed them that this had come from Satan. This view is not acceptable, because it must be one of two possibilities. Either the Prophet (ﷺ) uttered these words deliberately, and that is impermissible, because it would be disbelief (*kufr*), and because he was sent as one who reviles the idols, not one who praises them. Or Satan caused these words to be spoken by the tongue of the Prophet (peace be upon him) by compulsion, such that he could not refrain from them. This is also impossible, because Satan has no power to do that to others, as God says: *"Indeed, My servants, you have no authority over them"* [15:42]. So it is even more so with regard to him. Or these words flowed from his tongue by inadvertence and heedlessness. This too is rejected, because such heedlessness cannot occur to him while conveying revelation. If it were possible, the reliability of his words would be nullified. Furthermore, God said describing the one to whom it was revealed: *"Falsehood cannot come to it from before it or behind it"* [41:42], and He said: *"Indeed, it is We who sent down the Reminder, and indeed, We will be its guardian"* [15:9]. When these possibilities are invalid, only one remains: that he (peace be upon him) was silent at His words *"And Manat, the third, the other"* [53:20], so Satan spoke these words connected to the recitation of the Prophet (ﷺ). Thus it occurred to some that he (ﷺ) was the one who had uttered them, and this would be a casting into the recitation of the Prophet (ﷺ). Satan used to speak during the time of the Prophet (ﷺ) and his speech would be heard. It is narrated that he called out on the day of Uhud: "Indeed, Muhammad has been killed!" and he said on the day of Badr: "No one among the people will overcome you today, and I am a protector for you."

﴿Then God abolishes what Satan casts﴾, i.e., He removes it, nullifies it, and makes known that it came from Satan. ﴿Then God establishes His verses﴾, i.e., He confirms them and preserves them from the addition of anything by Satan. ﴿And God is Knowing﴾ of what He revealed to His Prophet and of Satan's intention, ﴿Wise﴾, not leaving it alone until He uncovers it and removes it.

Then he mentioned that this occurs so that God may make it a trial (*fitna*) for a people, by His words (p-449)

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 22, verse 53:

﴿That He may make what Satan casts a trial﴾ a test and an affliction ﴿for those in whose hearts is a disease﴾ doubt and hypocrisy ﴿and the hard-hearted﴾ they are the polytheists and the deniers, so that they increase in doubt and darkness through it ﴿And indeed the wrongdoers﴾ that is, the hypocrites and the polytheists. Its original form was "and indeed they," but the apparent noun was placed in the position of the pronoun, to pass judgment upon them with wrongdoing ﴿are in extreme dissension﴾ opposition ﴿far away﴾ from the truth.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 22, verse 54:

﴿And that those who have been given knowledge may know﴾ of God, His religion and the signs, ﴿that it [i.e., the Qur'an] is the truth from your Lord, so that they believe in it﴾ in the Qur'an, ﴿and their hearts humble themselves before it﴾ i.e., are at peace with it, ﴿and indeed God guides those who believe to a straight path﴾.

So they interpret what is ambiguous (mutashabih) in the religion by means of sound interpretations, and they seek for what is unclear in it the meaning that is required by the firm foundations (al-usul al-muhkama), so that bewilderment does not reach them and doubt does not overtake them.

Verse 55: "And those who disbelieve will not cease to be in doubt about it" — doubt (شَكٍّ) — "about it," meaning about the Qur'an or about the straight path (الصِراطِ المُسْتَقِيمِ), "until the Hour comes upon them suddenly" — unexpectedly (فَجْأةً) — "or there comes to them the punishment of a barren day."

He means: the Day of Badr. It is "barren" (عَقِيمٌ) in that the disbelievers have no relief or ease (فَرَجٌ أوْ راحَةٌ) in it, like the barren wind (الرِيحِ العَقِيمِ), which brings no good; or [it is barren in that it is] severe, with no mercy in it; or there is no like of it in the greatness of its matter, because of the fighting of the angels in it. And it is related from al-Dahhak that it is the Day of Resurrection, and that what is meant by "the Hour" is its preliminary signs (مُقَدِّماتُهُ).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 22, verses 56–57:

﴿And those who disbelieve and deny Our signs, those will have a humiliating punishment.﴾ Then He singled out a group from the first party with a virtue, so He said.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 22, verses 56–57:

﴿And those who disbelieve and deny Our signs, those will have a humiliating punishment.﴾ Then He singled out a group from the first party with a virtue, so He said.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 22, verse 58:

﴿Those who emigrated in the way of Allah﴾: they went out from their homelands striving (in struggle). ﴿Then were slain﴾ in the struggle. "Quttilū" (with the doubled ta', meaning "were slain" intensively) is the reading of Ibn 'Amir (al-Shami). ﴿Or died﴾ of natural causes (lit. "death by their own noses," ḥatf anfihim). ﴿Allah will surely provide for them a goodly provision.﴾ It has been said: the goodly provision is that which never ends, ever. ﴿And indeed Allah is the best of providers.﴾ Because He is the One who originates creation without a model, and who undertakes provision without wealth.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 22, verse 59:

﴿Surely He will admit them to an admission﴾ — read with a fatha on the mim by Madani (the reader of Madina). What is meant is Paradise, ﴿which they will be pleased with﴾, because in it is what the souls desire and the eyes delight in. ﴿And indeed Allah is All-Knowing﴾ of the circumstances of those who fulfilled their vow by fighting (in jihad), and of the hopes of those who died while awaiting (the fulfilment of a covenant), ﴿Forbearing﴾ in granting respite to those who fought against them in obstinacy.

It is narrated: "Some of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'O Prophet of Allah, these who were killed, we know what good Allah gave them. We too strive alongside you as they strove. So what will be for us if we die with you?' Then Allah revealed these two verses."

﴿That﴾: that is the matter. What follows it is a resumptive sentence (isti'naf, a new sentence not grammatically dependent on what precedes it). ﴿And whoever retaliates with the like of what he was afflicted with﴾: the initiating of the requital is called "punishment" (ʿuqūbah) because it is connected to it, in that the initiating is a cause and that (the requital) is caused by it. ﴿Then he is wronged again, God will surely help him﴾: that is, whoever repays with the like of the wrong done to him, and then is wronged after that, it is incumbent upon God to help him. ﴿Indeed God is Ever Pardoning﴾ who erases the traces of sins, ﴿Oft-Forgiving﴾ who covers all kinds of faults. The juxtaposition of the two attributes with the context of the verse indicates that the one who retaliates is being urged by God toward pardon and abandoning punishment, through His saying: ﴿But whoever pardons and makes reconciliation, his reward is with God﴾ [al-Shura: 40], and ﴿And that you pardon is nearer to piety﴾ [al-Baqarah: 237]. So since he did not prefer that and sought retribution, he has forgone what is better, and He guarantees His help for him in the second instance if he abandons pardon and takes vengeance upon the aggressor. He also alluded, along with this, to what was more fitting for him than pardon, by mentioning these two attributes. Or, by mentioning pardon and forgiveness, He indicates that He is capable of punishment, since no one is described as pardoning except one who is capable of its opposite, as it is said: "Pardon is in the state of power."

That is because Allah causes the night to enter into the day and causes the day to enter into the night, and because Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing. Meaning: that victory for the wronged is due to the fact that He is capable of whatever He wills. And among the signs of His power is that He causes the night to enter into the day and causes the day to enter into the night, i.e., He adds from this to that and from that to this. Or, it is because He is the Creator of the night and the day and the One who directs them, so nothing is hidden from Him of what takes place in them at the hands of His servants, of good and evil, of oppression and fairness. And He is All-Hearing of what they say, and hearing one thing does not distract Him from hearing another, even though voices in the day vary in the many kinds of languages. All-Seeing of what they do, and nothing is concealed from Him by anything in the nights, even though darkness follows one another.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 22, verse 62:

﴿That is because Allah is the Truth, and what they call upon besides Him is falsehood, and Allah is the Most High, the Great﴾ — read by ʿIraqi (Ibn ʿĀmir? no: the reading of the Iraqi readers) except Abu Bakr [ʿĀsim's transmitter] — ﴿besides Him is falsehood, and that Allah is the Most High, the Great﴾. That is, that attribute is due to His creating the night and the day, His encompassing of what passes within them, and His knowing what they say and do, because Allah is the Truth, whose divinity is established, and everything that is called a god besides Him is false in its claim, and there is nothing higher than Him in rank and greater than Him in authority.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (*Madarik al-Tanzil*) on surah 22, verse 63:

﴿Have you not seen that Allah sends down water from the sky﴾, meaning rain, ﴿so the earth becomes green﴾ with vegetation, ﴿after it had been black and dry﴾. The phrase is expressed in the imperfect (*mudari'*) form, and he did not say *fa-asbahat* (the past tense), in order to convey that the effect of the rain remains over time, one period after another. This is like when you say: "So-and-so has favored me, so I spend my evenings and mornings (*afrahu wa aghdu*) thankful to him." If you had said *faraha't wa ghadawt* (in the past tense), it would not have occupied that position.

As for ﴿fa-tusbih﴾ being in the nominative (*rafa'a*) and not in the subjunctive (*nasb*), this is because it is the answer to the interrogative. If it were in the subjunctive, the purpose would be lost, because its meaning is the affirmation of greening. With the subjunctive, it would turn into the negation of greening. This is like when you say to your companion: "Have you not seen that I have bestowed favors upon you so that you give thanks?" If you put it in the subjunctive, you negate his thanks and complain of his negligence in it. If you put it in the nominative, you affirm his thanks.

﴿Indeed, Allah is Subtle﴾, whose kindness or favor reaches everything, ﴿Aware﴾ of the interests and benefits of creation. Or, *al-Latif* means the one who is specially attentive to fine and subtle arrangement, *al-Khabir* the one who encompasses every small and great thing.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 22, verse 64:

﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth﴾ — in ownership (mulk) and in possession (milk). ﴿And indeed, Allah — He is the Self-Sufficient (al-Ghani)﴾ — the One who is independent through the perfection of His power, after the passing away of whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth. ﴿the Praiseworthy (al-Hamid)﴾ — the One who is praised for His favour before the praise of those who are in the heavens and those who are on the earth.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 22, verse 65:

﴿Have you not seen that Allah has subjected to you whatever is on the earth﴾ — of the cattle, made docile for riding on land; ﴿and the ship that runs upon the sea by His command﴾ — i.e., and of the vessels running upon the sea. Al-Fulk (the ship) is put in the accusative as a conjunction with "ma" (whatever), and "tajri" (runs) is its circumstantial clause (hal), i.e., He subjected to you the ship while it is running. ﴿And He holds back the sky from falling upon the earth﴾ — i.e., He preserves it from falling, ﴿except by His permission﴾ — by His command or by His will. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Kind (ra'uf) to mankind﴾ — by subjecting what is on the earth to them; ﴿Merciful (rahim)﴾ — by holding back the sky lest it fall upon the earth. He enumerated His bounties coupled with His names so that they would thank Him for His bounties and mention Him by His names. And it is related from Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on him, that the Greatest Name of Allah (ism Allah al-a'zam) is in these eight verses, and its reciters' supplications are granted without fail.

**"And it is He who gave you life"** — in the wombs of your mothers — **"then causes you to die"** — at the end of your appointed terms — **"then gives you life again"** — to bring you your recompense. **"Indeed, man is ungrateful"** — he is truly a denier of the various kinds of blessings He has poured out upon him and the diverse calamities He has warded off from him — **"or"** (p. 453) does not recognize the blessing of origination which brings him into existence, nor the blessing of extinction which brings him near to the promised [day], nor the blessing of resurrection which conveys him to the intended [goal].

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 22, verse 67:

﴿For every community﴾ of people of a religion ﴿We have appointed a rite﴾ whose explanation has already passed. This is a rebuttal of the view of those who say that slaughter is not part of God's sacred law, since it is the sacred law of every community. ﴿They are the ones who perform it﴾, acting upon it. ﴿So let them not dispute with you﴾, that is, let them not argue with you, and the meaning is: do not turn your attention to their words, and do not allow them to dispute with you ﴿concerning the matter﴾, the matter of slaughtered animals or of the religion. It was revealed when the polytheists said to the Muslims: "What is the matter with you that you eat what you kill, but do not eat what God kills?" meaning carrion. ﴿And invite﴾ people ﴿to your Lord﴾, to the worship of your Lord, ﴿for you are surely upon a straight guidance﴾, a upright path.

He did not mention the conjunction "wa" (and) in ﴿For every community﴾, unlike what preceded it, because that one occurred alongside the verses that are suitable to it concerning the matter of sacrificial rites, so it was joined to its sisters; whereas this one occurred alongside verses far removed from its meaning, so it did not find a conjunction to attach to.

"And if they dispute with you," out of contentiousness and obstinacy, as foolish people do, after your effort to ensure that there be no strife or disputation between you and them, "then say: Allah knows best what you do." That is: do not argue with them, and repel them with this statement. The meaning is: Allah knows your deeds and what you deserve in return for them, so He will recompense you for them. This is a warning and an admonition, but delivered with gentleness, softness and discipline, with which every obstinate person is answered.

Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection concerning that about which you used to differ. This is an address from Allah to both the believers and the disbelievers, meaning: He will separate you by reward and punishment. It is also a consolation to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for what he used to suffer from them.

Did you know that Allah knows what is in the heavens and the earth? ﴿Do you not know that Allah knows whatever is in the heavens and the earth?﴾ That is: how could what you do be hidden from Him? And it is known among the scholars of Allah that He knows everything that happens in the heavens and the earth. ﴿Indeed, that﴾, existing within them, ﴿is in a Book﴾, in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz), ﴿indeed, that is easy for Allah﴾. That is: His knowledge of all of that is easy for Him.

Then He pointed to the ignorance of the disbelievers in worshipping that which does not deserve worship, by His saying ﴿And they worship besides Allah that for which He has not sent down any authority﴾. "Yunazzil" is read by Makki and Basri (as yunazzil, with the verb in the form that makes it "sent down" in the active voice). ﴿authority﴾: proof and evidence. ﴿and of which they have no knowledge﴾: that is, in their worship of them they did not hold fast to any heavenly proof from the direction of revelation, nor was there any rational argument that led them to it. ﴿And for the wrongdoers there are no helpers﴾: for those who committed this kind of wrong there is no one who supports them or upholds their position.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 22, verse 72:

﴿And when Our clear revelations are recited to them, you recognize denial in the faces of those who disbelieve﴾, meaning: the Qur'an. ﴿You recognize denial in the faces of those who disbelieve﴾, i.e., the denial, through sullenness and aversion. Al-munkar is a verbal noun (maṣdar). ﴿They almost assault﴾ yabṭishūn (they attack), and al-saṭw is leaping forward and seizing. ﴿Those who recite Our revelations to them﴾ are the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions. ﴿Say: Shall I inform you of something worse than that?﴾ Worse than your rage at those who recite and your assault upon them, or than the aversion and distress you feel because of what is recited to you. ﴿The Fire﴾ is the predicate of an omitted subject, as if a questioner had asked, "What is it?" and it was answered: "The Fire," i.e., it is the Fire. ﴿Allah has promised it to those who disbelieve﴾ is a resumptive statement. ﴿And wretched is the destination﴾, the Fire.

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on Surah 22, verse 73:**

Since their claim that God has a associate was, in its strangeness and notoriety, like a proverb that is passed around, Allah the Exalted said: ﴿O mankind, a parable has been coined﴾ (ḍuriba, which is explained as bunna, "made clear"), ﴿so listen to it.﴾ (He gives this parable) for the sake of striking this example: ﴿Indeed, those you invoke﴾ (yadʿūna, read by Sahl and Yaʿqūb as tadʿūna) ﴿besides Allah﴾, as gods, ﴿will never create a fly﴾. Lan (never) is for emphasizing the negation of the future, and its emphasis here indicates that creating a fly is impossible for them, as if he had said: it is impossible that they create. The specification of the fly is because of its lowliness, weakness and repulsiveness. It was named dhubāb (fly) because whenever it is driven away (dhubba) out of repulsion, it returns out of arrogance (istikbār). ﴿Even if they gathered together﴾ for the creation of a fly. Its position is in the accusative as a circumstantial clause (ḥāl), as if it were said: it is impossible for them to create a fly, on condition that they all gather together for its creation and cooperate in it. This is among the most eloquent of what has been revealed in condemning the Quraysh for ignorance, since they ascribed divinity to (things) which necessitates power over all that is possible and comprehensive knowledge of all that is known, to images and statues, which are impossible to be able to create even the least and most humble of what Allah the Exalted has created, even if they gathered together for that purpose.

﴿And if the fly should snatch from them something﴾ (the second object of yasluban-hum), ﴿they could not recover it from it.﴾ That is: even if this least and most humble creature were to snatch something from them, and they gathered together to retrieve it from it, they would not be able to.

From Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that they used to smear them with saffron and put honey on their heads, and when the fly took it, the idols were unable to take it back. ﴿Weak is the seeker﴾, that is, the idol, which seeks what has been taken from it, ﴿and the sought﴾, the fly, which seeks what it has taken. This is like equating them with the fly in weakness. But if you examine closely, you will find the seeker weaker and weaker still, for the fly is a living animal, while (the idol) is inanimate; and the fly is victorious while that (the idol) is defeated.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 22, verse 74:

﴿They did not measure God with His true measure﴾: they did not know Him with His true knowledge, in that they made this weak idol a partner to Him. ﴿Indeed God is Strong, Mighty﴾: that is, God is capable and dominant, so how could the powerless and vanquished take as a likeness to Him? Or: He is strong in aiding His friends, and Mighty, exacting vengeance upon His enemies.

Allah chooses (يَصْطَفِي) — He selects (يَخْتارُ) — **from the angels messengers** (رُسُلا), such as Jibril, Mika'il, Israfil and others; **and from mankind** (رُسُلًا), such as Ibrahim, Musa, Isa and Muhammad (ﷺ) and others, peace be upon them all. This is a refutation of what they denied, namely that the messenger could be from among mankind, and a clarification that the messengers of Allah are of two kinds: an angel and a human being.

It was also said that it was revealed when they said: ﴿Has the Reminder been sent down upon him from among us?﴾ [Sad: 8]. ﴿Indeed, Allah is All-Hearing﴾ of their statement, ﴿All-Seeing﴾ of whom He chooses for His message; or, ﴿All-Hearing﴾ of the statements of the messengers regarding what the intellects accept, ﴿All-Seeing﴾ of the conditions of the nations in their rejection and acceptance.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 22, verse 76:

﴿He knows what is before them﴾: what has passed. ﴿And what is behind them﴾: what has not yet come, or what they have done and what they will do, or the affair of this world and the affair of the Hereafter. ﴿And to Allah are all matters returned﴾: that is, to Him all affairs are returned. One who has these attributes is not questioned about what He does, and no one has the right to object to His judgment, His arrangements, or His choice of messengers. "Turja'u" (is returned) is read by Ibn 'Amir (al-Shami), Hamzah and 'Ali.

O you who believe, bow down and prostrate yourselves, ﴿ya ayyuha alladhina amanu arka'u wa-sjudu﴾, in your prayer. And it was the case that when they first embraced Islam they would pray without bowing or prostrating, so they were commanded that their prayer be with bowing and prostration. In this there is evidence that deeds are not part of faith (īmān), and that this prostration is for prayer and not for recitation.

﴿Wa-'budu rabbakum﴾: worship your Lord, and direct your bowing and your prostration toward the Face of Allah, not toward an idol (ṣanam).

﴿Wa-f'alu al-khayr﴾: It has been said that since remembrance (dhikr) has a distinction over other acts of obedience, He first called the believers to prayer, which is pure remembrance, based on His saying, ﴿And establish prayer for My remembrance﴾ [Ṭā-Hā: 14]. Then He called them to worship other than prayer, such as fasting and pilgrimage (ḥajj) and others. Then He generalized the exhortation to all other good deeds. It has also been said that it refers to maintaining ties of kinship (ṣilat al-arḥām) and noble character (makārim al-akhlāq).

﴿La'allakum tufliḥun﴾: that is, so that you may succeed. Do all of this while you hope for success, not being certain of it, and do not rely on your deeds.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 22, verse 78:

﴿And strive﴾ is a command to fight (al-ghazw) or to struggle against the self and its desires (mujahadat al-nafs wa al-hawa), and this is the greater struggle (al-jihad al-akbar); or it is speaking a word of truth before an unjust ruler. ﴿In God's cause﴾ means: for the sake of God's essence and for His sake. ﴿With the struggle due to Him﴾, which is that one should not fear the blame of any blamer in God's cause. It is said: "he is the truth of a scholar and the earnestness of a scholar," meaning truly and earnestly, and from this comes ﴿haqq jihadihi﴾. The analogical form would have been "haqq al-jihad fihi" or "haqq jihadikum fihi," but the idiomatic construction (al-idafah) is used for the slightest connection and specification. Since the struggle is specific to God, in that it is undertaken for His sake and for His countenance, its annexation to Him is correct. It is also permissible to extend the adverbial (al-zarf) as in his saying (p-457):

"And on the day we witnessed Sulaym and Amir..."

He is the One ﴿who chose you﴾, selecting you for His religion and for supporting it. ﴿And He has not placed upon you any hardship (haraj) in religion﴾, meaning narrowness; rather He has granted you concessions in everything He has obligated you to, regarding purification, prayer, fasting and pilgrimage: tayammum, gesturing (in prayer), shortening, breaking the fast due to the excuse of travel, illness, and lack of a mount. ﴿The religion of your father Abraham﴾, i.e., follow the religion of your father; or it is in the accusative by way of specification, meaning: I mean by religion the religion of your father. He called him a father although he was not the father of the whole community, because he was the father of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and so he was a father to his community, since the community of the Messenger is in the position of his children. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I am to you only like a father." ﴿He named you Muslims﴾, i.e., God, based on the reading of Ubayy: "God named you." ﴿Before﴾ in the earlier Books, ﴿and in this﴾, i.e., in the Qur'an, meaning: He preferred you over all other nations and named you with this most noble name. ﴿That the Messenger may be a witness over you﴾ that he has conveyed to you the message of your Lord, ﴿and that you may be witnesses over mankind﴾ by conveying to them the messages of God which the Messengers conveyed to them. He singled you out with this honour and distinction. ﴿So establish the prayer﴾ with its obligations, ﴿and give the zakat﴾ with its conditions, ﴿and hold fast to God﴾, trust in God and rely upon Him, not upon prayer and zakat. ﴿He is your Protector﴾, i.e., your Owner, your Helper, and the One who manages your affairs. ﴿How excellent a Protector, and how excellent a Helper﴾, since He does not withhold your provision because of your disobedience. He is the Helper who assists you in your obedience, and whoever has Him as protector and helper has prospered. And God is the Granter of success to what is right.
